title: Knockout Drum

introduction.definition: A knockout drum removes liquid droplets from a gas stream — typically in flare systems. The gas slows down in the large drum so droplets settle by gravity and collect at the bottom; dry gas leaves for the flare and the liquid is pumped out.
key_points: Low gas velocity lets drops settle
Sized per API 521 for droplet size
introduction.summary: A flare knockout (KO) drum removes liquid droplets from gas going to a flare. The gas slows down in the large drum so droplets fall out by gravity and collect at the bottom; dry gas goes on to the flare and the liquid is pumped out. It prevents burning liquid "rain" from the flare.

video_tutorials.title: Knockout Drum — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Knockout Drum.
A knockout drum removes liquid droplets from a gas stream — typically in flare systems.
The gas slows down in the large drum so droplets settle by gravity and collect at the bottom; dry gas leaves for the flare and the liquid is pumped out.
Typical applications include flare and blowdown systems; compressor suction protection; fuel gas systems.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Knockout Drum — Operation

script.narration: How the Knockout Drum works.
Wet gas enters through the inlet and hits the diverter.
Gas slows down across the drum; droplets fall out.
Liquid collects at the bottom; level rises.
Dry gas leaves for the flare; liquid is pumped out.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Knockout Drum.
Check level and pump-out.
Test level alarms.
Internal inspection.
Watch for liquid carry-over to flare: burning rain, smoke. Common cause: high level, undersized drum.
Watch for freezing/hydrates: blockage. Common cause: cold expansion.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
